name: DEC PDP-11/20 minicomputer
summary: Digital Equipment Corporation's PDP-11/20, offered in January 1970 at $10,800, was a 16-bit minicomputer whose single UNIBUS linked processor, memory and peripherals.
description: Digital Equipment Corporation PDP-11/20 16-bit minicomputer with UNIBUS connecting processor, memory and peripherals.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: DEC faced new 16-bit rivals such as Data General, founded by former DEC engineers, and needed a modern design to compete.

evidence.supports: The contemporary report gives the $10,800 PDP-11/20 configuration and says customer orders were already booked.
The article describes the single asynchronous shared bus and notes Apollo guidance and GR-909 predecessors with related bus ideas.
